questions.stem: The largest freshwater lake in India by area is:
questions.explanation: Wular — largest freshwater lake in India, 30-260 km² (varies seasonally), in Bandipora district, J&K, fed by River Jhelum. Chilika (Odisha) is the largest LAGOON / brackish-water lake (1,165 km²). Vembanad (Kerala) is the longest lake (96 km), used for the famous Nehru Trophy snake-boat race. Loktak (Manipur) is famous for its floating phumdis. Wular is also a Ramsar site (1990).

questions.stem: The world's deepest freshwater lake — containing about 22% of Earth's surface freshwater — is:
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal — Siberia, Russia. Maximum depth 1,642 m (~1.6 km — deepest freshwater lake). Holds ~23,615 km³ water = ~22% of world's surface freshwater. UNESCO WHS 1996. ~25 million years old (oldest existing lake). Endemic species — Baikal seal (Pusa sibirica), the only freshwater seal. Caspian Sea is the largest lake (by area, 371,000 km²) but is brackish. Tanganyika — 2nd deepest (1,470 m) and 2nd by volume. Superior is the largest by surface area among freshwater lakes (82,000 km²).

options.option_text: A meandering river that gets cut off when the meander loop is severed

questions.explanation: Oxbow lake — crescent-shaped (named for the U-bend of an ox's yoke). Formation: a river meander loops tighter and tighter; eventually the river cuts a new direct channel across the neck of the loop; the abandoned bend becomes a still-water U-shaped lake. Common on flat floodplains — Ganga, Brahmaputra, Ravi all have many oxbow lakes. Glacial lakes (cirque, tarn) form by glacier carving; crater lakes by volcanic activity (e.g. Lonar Lake, Maharashtra, ~50,000 yrs old, formed by meteorite impact in basalt).

questions.stem: Lonar Lake — a circular saline-soda lake of meteoritic origin, ~50,000 years old, is in:
questions.explanation: Lonar Lake — Buldhana district, Maharashtra. Formed by a meteorite impact in basalt rock ~52,000 years ago — making it the only known hypervelocity impact crater in basalt on Earth. Diameter ~1.2 km; maximum depth 137 m. Both saline AND alkaline (a rare combination). Declared a Ramsar site in 2020. Near Aurangabad — about 175 km. Geologically and astrobiologically significant; ISRO and NASA have studied the site.

questions.stem: Match lake with state — which pairing is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Pulicat — Andhra Pradesh / Tamil Nadu border

questions.explanation: Kolleru is in ANDHRA PRADESH (between the deltas of Krishna and Godavari) — NOT Karnataka. Largest freshwater lake in Andhra; declared Ramsar site 2002; key habitat for migratory pelicans, painted storks. Sambhar — largest INLAND saline lake in India (Rajasthan). Pulicat — second largest brackish-water lagoon (after Chilika), AP-TN border. Dal — Srinagar, J&K, famous for shikaras + houseboats.

questions.stem: The largest lake in the world by area (though technically a lake, sometimes called a sea) is:
questions.explanation: Caspian Sea — endorheic (no outlet), 371,000 km² — bordered by 5 countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan). Brackish. Often called a 'sea' because of its size and salt content (~1.2%, about a third of seawater). Lake Superior is the largest FRESHWATER lake by area (82,100 km²). Lake Victoria — Africa, 2nd largest freshwater by area (68,800 km²); Tanganyika — 2nd longest. The 'lake vs sea' status of the Caspian was settled by the 2018 Convention as a 'special status' body, neither fully sea nor fully lake.

questions.stem: The Tso Lhamo / Tso Lhamu Lake — claimed to be one of the highest lakes in the world (~5,330 m) — is in:
questions.explanation: Tso Lhamo — North Sikkim, ~5,330 m above sea level, source of the Teesta River. Located near the China border; visit requires special permits. The fresh water of the lake is fed by glaciers and snowmelt. Other notable Sikkim lakes — Gurudongmar (5,210 m, sacred to Sikhs/Hindus/Buddhists), Tsomgo (3,750 m, popular tourism). Himalayan high-altitude lakes are sensitive indicators of climate change. Pangong Tso (Ladakh, 4,350 m) and Tso Moriri (4,522 m) are larger but lower than Tso Lhamo.
